Loop vs Graph：局部自治循环 vs 显式编排拓扑 §8.X

不要把 Loop 和 Graph 当成两代互相替代的技术。Loop 是一个 Agent 在局部任务中的自治控制模式；Graph 是把多个工作单元、决策边界和恢复路径组织成显式拓扑。

FIG.8.X

先把单个 Loop 做到可控，再在结构边界出现时拆成 Graph

默认从最小可控循环开始。只有当协调复杂度要求显式拓扑时，才增加 Graph 的控制流复杂度。

LOOP

一个连贯目标内的局部自治

Goal → Observe → Reason / Plan → Act → Verify → Stop or iterate。适合共享上下文、单一权限边界、明确验证方式与显式停止条件。
GRAPH

跨边界工作的显式协调

Router → bounded work units → branch / join → checkpoint → validation → recovery。适合并行分支、不同上下文或权限域、可审计决策点与独立恢复。
START

Bounded Agent Loop

先让状态、停止条件、验证和失败恢复可控。
BOUNDARY

结构性边界出现

并行 · 不同权限 · 不同上下文 · branch / join · checkpoint / resume · failure isolation · human approval
SPLIT

把边界拆成显式 Graph 节点与边

只增加解决真实协调问题所需的控制流复杂度。
UPGRADE什么时候从 Loop 升级为 Graph
看结构信号，而不是看流行词：并行轨道；不同 context / memory / permission；显式 branch / join；checkpoint / resume；failure isolation；需要审计的控制点；高风险动作的人审边界。
NODEGraph Node 不等于 Agent Loop
节点可以是 deterministic function、retrieval step、tool execution、policy gate、human approval、sub-workflow，也可以是 agent loop。Graph 定义的是拓扑，不要求每个节点都自治。

Coding Agent Engineering：从写代码转向定义、指挥与验证 §8.7

Coding Agent 并没有消除软件工程流程，而是重新分配工程师的注意力：更少时间花在手写代码，更多时间花在决定做什么、设计架构、写清 Spec、校准 Agent 自主权、验证结果，以及把反馈带回前面的阶段。它们也可以承担数据分析、系统操作等非代码执行任务，因此真正需要治理的是整个 execution loop，而不只是 code generation。

FIG.8.7

Coding Agent 工作流仍然是软件工程，只是执行者与注意力分布发生变化

Planning → Execution → Deployment & Monitoring 不是一次性流水线。验证或监控失败时，应该返回更早的阶段修正 Spec、架构、上下文或执行计划。

1 · PLAN

研究、理解代码库、写 Spec、拆计划

先明确需求、技术设计、架构、约束与验收标准，再审视关键假设、安全风险与是否过度设计。Greenfield 原型可以轻量；复杂 Brownfield 系统需要更严格的规划与验证。
2 · EXECUTE

构建、测试、验证，并校准自主权

决定哪些步骤需要高频人机往返，哪些可以委托成较大工作块；同时管理上下文、权限、并行 Agent 与人的注意力预算。
3 · DEPLOY / OBSERVE

通过 Gate 上线，再用证据驱动下一轮

使用 CI/CD 与必要的人审 Gate 部署；让 Agent 协助观察日志、发现问题、提出修复，但高风险副作用仍需要明确权限、验证与回滚边界。
ITERATIVE, NOT LINEAR

Verification 失败不只是“再生成一次代码”。它可能意味着 Spec 不清、架构假设错误、上下文过期、任务拆分不合理或验证器本身不够好。Monitoring 暴露的问题同样可能要求回到 Planning，而不是只在生产环境里打补丁。

五项核心能力：真正的稀缺资源是工程判断

能力工程师真正要决定什么薄弱时的典型失败
Directing the workflow规划多深、何时开始执行、何时回退、何时保留 Human Ownership；如何选择架构、写 planning artifacts / Spec，并在速度、成本、技术风险与人工投入之间权衡。Agent 很快地把错误问题做完，或者在没有验收标准的情况下持续漂移。
Enabling agent autonomy每个阶段需要多少自主权；什么时候交互式盯紧，什么时候委托大块工作或 bounded loop，什么时候并行多个 Agent，以及如何管理 Context、权限、Gate 与 Blast Radius。把“自主运行时间长”误当成熟度，导致错误更快扩散、上下文失真或高风险动作失控。
Reviewing the work什么证据能证明完成：自动测试、行为与功能验证、截图或 Artifact、Eval Set、LLM-as-judge、Agentic Code Review、安全/架构审计，以及哪些关键点仍需要人工判断。Agent 自己宣布完成就被当成完成，或者测试只验证实现细节而没有验证真实目标。
Customizing the agent and its environment如何用 Skills、Plugins、MCP、Hooks 与项目级说明文件提供工具和 Standing Context；如何跨 Session 保存必要状态、沉淀复盘，并清理过时能力与 Agent-generated debt。每个 Session 都重新解释项目，Agent 频繁丢背景，工具权限过宽，旧 Skill 与新模型能力互相冲突。
Coding agent foundations理解 Agent 如何搜索代码、检索上下文、使用 Context Window、调用工具与 Subagent，以及 Harness 如何约束模型行为与上下文成本。看不出 Agent 为什么过度设计、遗漏约束、提前停止或在错误上下文里继续自信执行。
AUTONOMY自主权是阶段级控制变量，不是成熟度徽章
高自主权适合可验证、可回滚、Blast Radius 小的工作；高风险规划、权限变更、生产副作用和不可逆动作应保留更强的人类 Gate。
CONTEXTContext 是工程基础设施，不是一次性 Prompt
项目约束、架构假设、代码风格、数据访问模式和当前 Spec 应有稳定、可维护的载体。需求中途变化时，必须更新 Agent 实际读取的 Context，而不是只在人的脑中更新。
CANONICAL RULE

A coding agent is not an autonomous coder; it is an execution component inside a human-directed, testable, permissioned engineering loop. Verification 属于 Execution 本身，而不是完成之后才补做的后处理。

CANONICAL RULE

Coding agents lower the cost of implementation; they raise the value of specification, verification, and engineering judgment.

PITFALL

Long-running autonomy is not a quality metric. 真正重要的是：目标是否清晰、Context 是否正确、权限是否受控、Verification 是否可信，以及工程师是否知道什么时候介入、回退或停止。

CH08 → CH09 · CONTROL PLANE

Chapter 08 负责 Coding Agent 的 Build / Execute：规划、委托、工具、状态、自主权与恢复。Chapter 09 负责外层 Reliability Control Plane：Validation、Eval、Observability、Release Gate、Monitoring 与生产证据回流。Reviewing the work 因此不应停在本地 Code Review，而要一直延伸到生产后的 regression protection。

Agent Project Engineering Lifecycle：从 Demo 到可维护系统 §8.P

能调用模型和 Tool 只说明执行链路存在。真正可维护的 Agent 项目还需要任务契约、仓库规范、运行拓扑、能力契约、状态生命周期、评估证据和生产反馈。

FIG.8.P1 · AGENT PROJECT ENGINEERING LIFECYCLE

十个教学步骤，收敛成五个工程阶段

这不是一次性的 waterfall。Eval、Trace 与 Production Failure 都可以把工作送回更早的错误层。

DEFINE

Task Contract + Repository Contract + Architecture

Goal · Input · Output · Boundary · Success Criteria；再明确目录、测试命令、依赖/Secret 规则、模块职责和失败路径。
BUILD

Agent · Tools · Skills · Context / Memory · Prompt

Agent 负责不确定判断；Workflow 负责显式控制；Tool 提供单一能力；Skill 固化方法；State/Memory 管信息生命周期；Prompt 作为版本化行为配置。
VERIFY

Test + Eval

Test 验证程序契约；Eval 验证任务行为。固定 Dataset 让模型、Prompt、Skill 与 Workflow 版本可以被真正比较。
OPERATE

Deploy · Trace · Monitor

把 request、workflow state、Agent decision、Tool I/O、版本、Token、Latency、Cost 与 Task Outcome 连到同一条可诊断链路。
LEARN ↺

Root Cause → Dataset → Fix → Regression

生产证据应回到最早错误层：错误 State 修 State；错误 Tool 修 Tool；过时数据源修数据源；不是所有问题都回去改 Prompt。
工程目标

Make uncertain model behavior reliably serve a bounded, testable, observable business task.

FIG.8.P2 · RESPONSIBILITY BOUNDARIES

别把所有东西都叫 Agent

长期可维护性来自责任边界：谁负责判断、谁负责执行、谁保存状态、谁验证成功。

组件 负责什么 不应该偷偷负责什么

Skill经过验证的可复用任务方法协议或最终授权

Coding Agent 的项目指令文件应保持精炼，并指向真正的架构、测试和产品文档。以 Codex 为例，AGENTS.md 是官方支持的项目指令机制，但它不是所有 Agent 工具的统一标准。

FIG.8.P3 · AGENT ENGINEER CAPABILITY STACK

不是会几个框架，而是能不能把业务目标交付成可运营系统

四层能力形成一条闭环：业务定义目标，架构承载执行，可靠性提供证据，交付让系统持续演进。

1 · BUSINESS

业务拆解与流程设计

KPI · current workflow · automation boundary · human gate · exception path · Task Contract。不要先问用什么框架，先问成功是什么。
2 · ARCHITECTURE

运行时与能力架构

Tool / schema · Workflow · Agent · State · Context · Memory · Routing · Permission · failure semantics
3 · RELIABILITY

评估、可观测性与稳定性

task success · tool failure · latency · cost/success · human escalation · trace · alert · fallback · regression gate
4 · DELIVERY

工程交付与持续迭代

versioning · CI/CD · environment separation · rollout · rollback · runbook · incident diagnosis · production learning
BUSINESS PROBLEM

“Support cost is too high”

先转成 bounded outcome / KPI / automation boundary。
SYSTEM

Task Contract → Runtime Architecture

选择 Workflow / Agent / Tool / State，而不是让框架反向定义业务。
EVIDENCE

Eval → Trace → Release Gate

证明任务成功、失败位置、成本和风险，而不是“感觉还不错”。
PRODUCTION LEARNING ↺

Operate → Diagnose → Regression → Improve

能力边界

Agent engineering competence is the ability to turn an ambiguous business objective into a bounded, testable, observable, operable system.

版本兼容

模型升级后 Prompt 是否仍可用，不能靠假设；固定 regression suite 后再比较 task success、safety、latency 与 cost。

Agent Architecture Selection：Pattern，不是七档成熟度 §8.AS

Single Agent、ReAct、Plan & Execute、Multi-Agent、Route + Skill、Shared State 与 Graph Workflow 不是同一维度的互斥架构。生产系统通常组合它们，真正的选型依据是控制流、状态、权限、恢复、成本与延迟。

FIG.8.AS1 · AGENT ARCHITECTURE PATTERN SPACE

“七种架构”其实分属五个控制维度

不要问“我属于哪一档”，而要问“我的系统在哪些维度需要更强控制”。

Long-Running Multi-Agent Handoff：接力必须先验证再提交 §8.S

长周期 Multi-Agent 的关键不是让每个 Agent 自己记住做到哪，而是让 Agent 可以随时消失，而 Workflow State、已验证 Artifact 和合法状态转移仍然持续存在。

FIG.8.S1 · DURABLE HANDOFF PROTOCOL

Candidate ≠ Committed Artifact；Agent 说 done ≠ Workflow 已推进

01 · READ

Committed State + Versioned Inputs

Worker 读取 durable workflow state、revision、owner/lease 与已经提交的 input artifact，不直接把上一 Agent 的自由文本当作事实。
02 · PRODUCE

Candidate Artifact

Agent 在 bounded task 内工作，输出 typed candidate artifact；此时它还不能让下游开始。
03 · VALIDATE

Schema → Semantic → Integrity → Acceptance

先检查结构可解析，再检查业务 invariant，再确认引用的文件/证据真实存在，必要时验证实际任务目标是否达成。
04 · COMMIT

Artifact Commit + Atomic State Transition

验证通过后把 Artifact 标为 authoritative，并用 CAS、single writer、transaction 或 workflow engine 提交合法 transition。
05 · PUBLISH

Next Task Becomes Runnable

只有 committed state 才发布给下游；失败则 repair、retry 或 escalate，不让 invalid candidate 静默传播。
核心顺序

produce → validate → commit → publish downstream

Loop vs Graph: Local Autonomy vs Explicit Orchestration Topology §8.X

Do not treat loops and graphs as two generations of competing technology. A loop is a local autonomous control pattern for an agent; a graph is an explicit topology for organizing work units, decision boundaries, and recovery paths.

FIG.8.X

Make the single loop controllable first; split into a graph only when structural boundaries appear

Start with the smallest controllable loop. Add graph-level control-flow complexity only when coordination complexity requires explicit topology.

LOOP

Local autonomy around one coherent goal

Goal → Observe → Reason / Plan → Act → Verify → Stop or iterate. Best when context is shared, the permission boundary is unified, verification is clear, and the stopping condition is explicit.
GRAPH

Explicit coordination across structural boundaries

Router → bounded work units → branch / join → checkpoint → validation → recovery. Best for parallel branches, different context or permission domains, auditable decision points, and independent recovery.
START

Bounded Agent Loop

First make state, stopping conditions, verification, and failure recovery controllable.
BOUNDARY

A structural boundary appears

parallelism · different permissions · different contexts · branch / join · checkpoint / resume · failure isolation · human approval
SPLIT

Split the boundary into explicit graph nodes and edges

Add only the control-flow complexity needed to solve a real coordination problem.
UPGRADEWhen to upgrade from a loop to a graph
Look for structural signals, not trend vocabulary: parallel tracks; different context, memory, or permission domains; explicit branch / join; checkpoint / resume; failure isolation; auditable control points; and human approval boundaries for high-risk actions.
NODEA graph node is not necessarily an agent loop
A node can be a deterministic function, retrieval step, tool execution, policy gate, human approval, sub-workflow, or an agent loop. A graph defines topology; it does not require every node to be autonomous.

Coding Agent Engineering: From writing code to specifying, directing, and verifying §8.7

Coding agents do not remove the software-engineering workflow; they redistribute engineering attention. Less time is spent typing code, while more time moves to deciding what to build, designing the architecture, writing a clear spec, calibrating agent autonomy, verifying results, and feeding later evidence back into earlier stages. They can also perform non-code execution such as data analysis and system operations, so the engineering problem is to govern the whole execution loop rather than code generation alone.

FIG.8.7

The coding-agent workflow is still software engineering; what changes is who executes and where human attention goes

Planning → Execution → Deployment & Monitoring is not a one-way pipeline. When verification or monitoring fails, return to an earlier stage to revise the spec, architecture, context, or execution plan.

1 · PLAN

Research, understand the codebase, write the spec, decompose the plan

Clarify requirements, technical design, architecture, constraints, and acceptance criteria before execution. Then interrogate assumptions, security risks, and overengineering. A greenfield prototype may need a light spec; a complex brownfield system needs much more rigorous planning and validation.
2 · EXECUTE

Build, test, verify, and calibrate autonomy

Decide which steps need tight human-agent iteration and which can be delegated as larger work units. At the same time, manage context, permissions, parallel agents, and the finite budget of human attention.
3 · DEPLOY / OBSERVE

Deploy through gates, then use evidence to drive the next iteration

Deploy through CI/CD and human gates where appropriate. Agents can watch logs, surface issues, and propose fixes, but high-risk side effects still need explicit permission, verification, and rollback boundaries.
ITERATIVE, NOT LINEAR

A verification failure is not merely a signal to regenerate code. It may reveal an unclear spec, a wrong architecture assumption, stale context, poor task decomposition, or an inadequate verifier. Problems found in monitoring may likewise require returning to planning rather than patching production locally.

CANONICAL RULE

Coding agents lower the cost of implementation; they raise the value of specification, verification, and engineering judgment.

03 · VALIDATE

Schema → Semantic → Integrity → Acceptance

FIG.8.T1 · CANCELLATION SCOPE

Cancelling a parent scope stops owned descendants; cancelling one child should not automatically kill siblings or the whole session.

MODEL

Stream / Retry / Backoff

TOOLS

Tool Batch / Tool Child

dispatch boundary · per-tool child signal · no new calls after cancel
OS / REMOTE JOB

Owned Execution Tree

process group · container job · browser session · remote cancel handle
SUBTASK

Foreground vs Detached

Foreground work usually inherits the parent; background work needs an explicit independent lifetime and cancel handle.
Core rule

Every blocking boundary must either accept cancellation directly or race against a cancellation signal.

FIG.8.T2 · INTERRUPTED TOOL TRUTH MODEL

After interruption, determine how far the tool executed before deciding to retry

NOT STARTED

Rejected / Cancelled Before Run

No side effect occurred; repair the protocol with a cancelled/rejected result and make a new decision.
STARTED · ABORTED

Partial / Unknown Effect

The tool started, so the runtime cannot claim it never ran; inspect files, processes, remote systems, or business state.
RESULT LOST

Completed? Ack Missing

The remote action may have committed even though the local result was lost; reconcile before any retry.
COMPLETED

Trusted Result Available

A complete trustworthy result is available and can be committed into conversation or workflow state normally.
SIDE-EFFECT BOUNDARY

Cancellation changes control flow; it does not retroactively erase side effects.

TRANSCRIPT REPAIR

Synthetic tool results repair the provider protocol. They must encode the real execution state rather than falsely claiming no execution merely to make the next API request valid.

FIG.8.T3 · USER CONTROL SEMANTICS

Cancel, steer, and follow-up are not the same event

CANCEL

Terminate Current Scope

Stop new work → terminate owned execution → reconcile → repair protocol → become quiescent.
STEER

Change Next Decision

Inject at a safe action/result boundary; already-observed tool work and side effects still belong in the next decision.
FOLLOW-UP

Queue After Completion

Start the new request only after the current run finishes its pending work—useful for 'after this, do that.'
SAFE INJECTION BOUNDARY

tool_use → tool_result → steering → next model call

Do not inject arbitrary user messages into an unresolved tool protocol unit; first restore a coherent action/result state.
Final rule

Cancellation is complete only when the execution scope is quiescent and its state is trustworthy.

FIG.8.T4 · CANCELLATION LIFECYCLE

The UI may show Cancelling immediately, but the runtime should not mark the run CANCELLED yet

RUNNING

Work Is Active

CANCEL_REQUESTED

TERMINATING

Abort Requests · Stop Tools · Kill Owned Jobs

RECONCILING

Repair Transcript · Verify Side Effects

QUIESCENT

CANCELLED / FAILED / HUMAN ACTION

cancel_ack_latency measures how fast the runtime acknowledges cancellation; cancel_to_quiescence_latency measures how long it takes to actually stop and return to trustworthy state.

Current OpenAI Codex source uses hierarchical CancellationToken values and, for one-shot exec cancellation, terminates the process group, waits a 50ms grace period, then force-kills remaining members. Current Pi documentation separates abort, steer, and follow-up semantics. Anthropic's current Tool Use documentation requires a complete tool_use/tool_result protocol, and its TypeScript BetaToolRunner supports AbortSignal. These are implementation evidence; the durable rules remain vendor-neutral.
